finding.claim: With permitSetMultiParamEntries enabled, object parameter keys are wrapped in backticks without escaping embedded backticks, so an attacker-chosen key breaks out of the identifier and injects SQL. Values are escaped but keys are not.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled object keys, e.g. a parsed JSON request body passed as a query parameter (conn.query('UPDATE t SET ?', req.body)). Precondition: the application enables the opt-in option permitSetMultiParamEntries and passes a user-shaped object.
finding.sink: Query text sent via COM_QUERY: out.writeString('`' + key + '`') at text-encoder.js:135

trace.note: this.encoder.writeParam(out, value, ...) for each placeholder value
plain object that is not GeoJSON and permitSetMultiParamEntries is true goes to the key/value expansion branch
for (let key in value) iterates the attacker-supplied keys, including inherited enumerable ones
key concatenated into '`'+key+'`' and written raw, with no replace(/`/g,'``') and no allowlist

finding.guards_checked: Values go through writeParam and are escaped. Keys have no check. Compare utils.escapeId at lib/misc/utils.js:91-106, which does double backticks, but it is not applied here. The option is off by default.

finding.claim: The client-side escape() helper, used by pool/connection .escape and the pipelined/prepare fallback, has the same flaw. With permitSetMultiParamEntries, object keys are interpolated inside backticks unescaped, giving SQL injection through a crafted key.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled object keys passed to escape() or to a query whose parameter is built from request data. Precondition: permitSetMultiParamEntries is enabled.
finding.sink: Returned SQL fragment: out += '`' + key + '`=' at utils.js:213, later concatenated into SQL

trace.note: permitSetMultiParamEntries branch of escapeParameters for plain objects
for (let key in value) takes attacker-controlled keys

finding.guards_checked: escapeId, which doubles backticks and rejects NUL, exists in the same file but is not called here. Values are escaped via escapeString. Off by default. Also note that line 214 uses `this.escape` inside an arrow function, where `this` is module.exports, which may work.
